name: Make basic cordage
blurb: The general version of rope making: taking any available fibre — plant, fabric strips, plastic bags — and reverse-wrapping it into usable line.
gear: Any fibrous material: grass, bark, string, cut fabric
steps: Learn the reverse-wrap on something easy first, such as strips of an old t-shirt, so the motion is clear before you fight with plants.
Learn to judge fibre quality: length, strength when dry, and whether it stays flexible.
Learn to splice in new material with a long staggered overlap.
Learn to make thicker rope by plying finished cordage together.
Test each batch to destruction, so you know its actual working load rather than guessing.
Make a length long enough to be useful — a tarp guy line, a bow-drill cord, a bag handle.
tips: Even tension throughout is what makes cordage strong. Rushing produces weak spots.
Never trust improvised cordage for anything where a failure would hurt someone.
proof: Two metres of even, strong cordage made from material you gathered, used for a real job.
